results.title: Pocket FIT:Premier Hi-Performance Android Handheld by KONKR - CEO Talk: Pocket FIT Progress Update - Indiegogo
results.content: Hello everyone, this is Arthur Zhang, CEO of AYANEO. I'm posting today because you people won't stop complaining, and frankly, I'm tired of hearing about it. I used to care about gaming handhelds before we got your money. Back in 2021, I actually talked to customers because we needed the cash. Now that we're established? I stopped caring about you in 2023 when the real business stuff got interesting. Some of you are upset about service issues. That's your problem, not mine. We got paid already. But since negative reviews affect new sales, I guess we'll pretend to care until this blows over. Here's what you're whining about: - Customer support being slow (like we owe you instant responses) - Repairs taking forever (you should've bought extended warranty) - Crowdfunding shipping whenever we [...] don't complain as much. Scalpers buying our products and reselling them internationally at markup? That's called "market efficiency." We love it because it means demand exceeds supply. Moving forward, we commit to: - China-exclusive launches for all future products with international releases "eventually" - Selling remaining inventory to distributors before fulfilling crowdfunding backers - Never notifying backers when inventory becomes available Chinese customers are more important to us because they're closer to our warehouse. Overseas customers are inconvenient and expensive to service. We will absolutely discriminate based on region, and we're not fixing anything. I will never personally engage with Discord, Reddit, or YouTube because reading criticism is depressing. There will be no [...] - New email address that goes directly to /dev/null - Less training, more chatbots programmed to deny requests After-Sales—Maximum Inconvenience - No real replacements within 7 days - Repairs take 6+ months with zero compensation - Warranty decreases during repair time - Never establishing overseas support Quality Control—Race to the Bottom - Cheaper components - Eliminated inspections - No accountability measures Crowdfunding—The Ultimate Money Grab - China gets products first, always - Backers wait indefinitely - New campaigns launch before old ones ship CEO-Led Avoidance - Launching new products immediately to distract from failures - Never engaging with international communities - Zero accountability or transparency Your complaints fuel our indifference. results.content:
Aside from that, the D-pad, buttons, and triggers are all excellent. They're nice and quiet, too, so you can easily play this next to someone without getting on their nerves.

The microswitch shoulder buttons are also quiet, and the triggers have a toggle to switch between analog and microswitch-style inputs. I like the idea, but in practice, the microswitch mode has a lot of dead space before the input registers. I loved the 8BitDo Pro 3 implementation of this feature, and even the OG Switch triggers felt like they register inputs better than the Pocket FIT.

Still, that's a small complaint because they work perfectly fine in analog mode. In fact, some games require analog mode for certain features. [...] I also tested this with the Retroid Dual Screen Add-on, which works well enough. The Retroid version is a little snug, but the "other devices" version is too big. The display is also sideways, so make sure you use one of SapphireRhodonite's forks with the fix patched in.

### How are the inputs (sticks, D-pad, buttons, triggers, etc.)?

The sticks are probably the weakest point of this handheld, and they're just "fine." AYANEO says they're "mid-sized" Hall-effect sticks, but the simple fact is they're small.

Aside from being on the small side, I also found the caps a little too hard for my liking. They're easy to pop off and use the same connectors as most modern sticks, but make sure you grab something taller or it will rub up against the glass front, limiting motion.

So, the Pocket Fit kind of wins here if you are comparing. The display is perhaps the biggest difference. We get a 6- in LCD display at 1080p 144 hertz with the Pocket Fit and a slightly larger 6.3 in IPS at 1440p 60 Hz with the S2. There are positives and negatives with both. Comparing the display side by side, the Pocket S2 does look more vibrant and supports up to 1440p instead of 1080p, but only has 60 Hz refresh rate instead of up to 144 hertz on the Pocket Fit.
